0.content: Wriothesley was taken in as an abandoned infant by a "host family", a loving couple who raised many children together. As each child grew up, they were placed with "families of greater means" and new young children arrived. He considered himself extremely lucky, and so did his siblings. Then he learned the truth: the children were raised "as livestock" and sold, and those who did not sell or who discovered the secret were "disposed of". He was not the first to find out. Too young and weak to fight adults, he fled, survived on the streets and came back armed. He killed both parents and set the remaining children free. He told the Traveler that his parents had built "a facade of joy" and kept power through cruelty, which is why the Beret Society struck him so hard.

1.content: He woke handcuffed to a hospital bed. Asked his name, he took "Wriothesley" from an old person's obituary rather than keep the name his foster parents had given him. At trial he confessed everything and added details so there was no room for argument, yet lawyers still debated orphan precedents and clemency. Furina left early, bored by his guilty plea. When the official recording his sentence asked his birthday, he answered "...Today": his official birthday, November 23, is that day.

2.content: When Wriothesley arrived, Meropide's Credit Coupons bought almost anything: drugs, fixed fights, loyalty, even a life. The administrator of the day used the Coupons to control inmates. Wriothesley built capital in the unregulated underground fights, invested it, and quietly held more Coupons than the rest of the Fortress combined, along with a reputation for fairness. The administrator emptied his account in one night. Wriothesley turned that into a cause and publicly challenged him to a duel "in the name of fairness, justice, and order"; no inmate or guard objected. The administrator fled, sparing Wriothesley more blood on his hands, on the very day his sentence ended. With no one left to sign his exit papers, he walked into the central office and took over.

3.content: Sigewinne, the Melusine head nurse, has known Wriothesley since he arrived as a scrawny teenager who refused anaesthetic for stitches ("an impressive little grown-up"). She sometimes slipped it into his tea and stitched him while he slept. He calls her a nurse with every virtue of her profession and enforces an unwritten rule: anyone rude to her is punished extra harshly. She nags him about drinking too much tea; he says her milkshakes taste of "desolation". She and her Melusine friends bet on who can put the most stickers on his things, and he pretends not to mind, because he does not.

4.content: Neuvillette presided over the young Wriothesley's case, followed his progress through Sigewinne's letters, and later conferred the title of Duke. At the ceremony he seemed more pleased than Wriothesley himself: "You have found something you wish to do at last, I see." He calls Wriothesley trustworthy, says he fought hard for the title, and will not explain further. They now cooperate as peers. Neuvillette arranged the Traveler's undercover stay, sealed the Primordial Sea at the gate, and works cases with the Duke.

key: If a man will not work
5.comment: Wriothesley: The hidden rules of the Fortress
5.content: The Fortress is legally autonomous: its inmates are technically exiles, and the Court has little oversight beyond the Gardes it lends. It is also a vast factory, so Wriothesley runs it on "Mora and manpower" and gladly meets the Maison Gestion's strict paperwork for his best customer, the Palais. He set three unwritten rules to teach inmates the worth of health and Coupons. Work non-stop and a mysterious restorative meal (Sigewinne's secret cooking) appears. Bet on both fighters in the Ring and you are served a blood-red test flavour of Fonta. And mistreat the head nurse at your peril. Many inmates choose to stay after their sentences end.

6.comment: Wriothesley: The sluice gate and the Wingalet
6.content: Only the Administrator may enter the Fortress's forbidden zone, where a giant sluice gate stands. Its gauge never moved when he first saw it; over the past year it crept into the red. After Freminet was poisoned by Primordial Seawater, Wriothesley concluded the gate was holding back the Primordial Sea from swallowing Fontaine. He explained that the first Fortress was built by repentant exiles under the old Hydro Archon Egeria to guard this secret. Inspired by Remurian legend, he had his technical consultants Jurieu (once Edwin Eastinghouse's assistant) and Lourvine build a huge escape ship, the Wingalet, and kept it secret to avoid a riot. When the gate failed he froze the surge, Clorinde shot the control panel to drop the backup gates, and he sent the Traveler for Neuvillette.
